summary: The upper Warren Landing range marks the west side of the Nelson River mouth: a wooden front tower of 1908, a steel skeleton rear, seasonal, reached only by boat.

structures.note: 31 ft (9.4 m) to the lantern ventilator in 1908; Rowlett gives a 6 m (19 ft) tower; white square tower with orange vertical stripe (CCG); Rowlett says red stripe
Enclosed wooden back tower, 12.2 m (40 ft), in 1908; now steel skeleton (Rowlett); 240 m (260 yd) north of the front light

access.note: Accessible only by boat; site open, tower closed (Rowlett)

events.note: Hugh McDonald appointed keeper of the Warren Landing ranges (14 August or 14 September 1907, depending on the report); the 1908 statement gives 25 August 1905 (cite 11)
Two pairs of range lights erected at the mouth of the Nelson River; the upper pair's front tower 9.4 m (31 ft) and back tower 12.2 m (40 ft), both enclosed wooden towers
Back light moved to a new site; William Dewar of Warren Landing paid $275 (Lighthouse Friends); Department works list for 1911 has the same move at Warren's Landing
Canada Post flag-definitive lighthouse stamp shows the upper front range (Lighthouse Friends)

keepers.name: Hugh McDonald
keepers.note: Keeper of both Warren Landing range pairs (listed as "Warren Landing ranges"). Appointed 14 August 1907 (1911 report) or 14 September 1907 (1914 report); Lighthouse Friends gives 1908 to 1924. 1908 statement (cite 11, scan p.199, row matched on the page image): Warren's Landing, appointed 25 August 1905. Not reconciled with the 1907 dates.

keepers.name: J. Robertson
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives "J. Robertson" and once "Keeper Roberts"; responsible through at least 1937. Not checked against a Department list (the corpus ends in 1924).

notes_for_editor: 1) Stripe colour: CCG says orange; Rowlett says red. The story gives both. 2) Heights: 1908 front tower 31 ft (9.4 m) and light 33 ft (10.1 m) above the lake; CCG focal height now 9.0 m and structure 5.9 m; Rowlett 6 m (19 ft) tower. Rear: 40 ft (12.2 m) enclosed in 1908; CCG structure 14.0 m, Rowlett 14 m (46 ft) skeletal. No source explains the changes. 3) The back-light move: Lighthouse Friends dates it 1910 (Dewar paid $275); the 1911 report's Warren's Landing row (scan p.70) is matched by position: 'Moving back light to a new site' and 'Wm. Dewar, Warren's Landing, Man' sit in separate OCR columns. Another entry, 'Moving back range lightmast to a new site' (scan p.65), names no station and is not used. 4) The 1908 'supervision' line is OCR-garbled (see lower-range notes); the cost sentence is taken as covering all four towers. 5) Lighthouse Friends' 2007 stamp fact is not checked against Canada Post or a catalogue. 6) Storms: no wreck or rescue at Warren Landing turned up in the corpus, so the chapter is omitted. 7) Record point for the upper front (Wikidata 53.694446, -97.870521) is about 34 m east of CCG 1622 (53 41 40.0 N, 097 52 12.0 W); not corrected, flagged only. 7) Checked on the page image (report of the Chief Engineer, printed p.63, scan p.70): the Warren's Landing row reads 'Moving back light to a new site | Contract | Wm. Dewar, Warren's Landing, Manitoba | 275 00'; the table sits under an 'ONTARIO—Continued' heading, but the station is named Warren's Landing (Manitoba). The story now cites the row with its $275.00 expenditure. 8) The 1908 statement of lightkeepers (scan p.199, printed p.190) gives Hugh McDonald at Warren's Landing appointed 25 August 1905; the 1911 and 1914 reports give 1907. Not reconciled. 9) The 1908 cost sentence (scan p.89) gives one cost for the towers; the story no longer says four towers cost it. 10) The 1914 McDonald entry (scan p.77) was read on the page image: 'H. McDonald, Sept. 14, 1907'. 11) CCG 1622 (front) and 1623 (rear) were read from the extracted list: front focal height 9.0, structure 5.9, orange stripe; rear focal height 15.0, structure 14.0, seasonal. Rowlett gives a red stripe for the front. Not imaged: the 1911 Warren Landing Ranges row (scan p.256) reads 'Hugh McDonald . . Aug. 14, 1907' on one OCR line in a row pattern that matches the 1914 image; the 1910 report (scan p.271) gives the same Aug. 14, 1907 on the same line.
